description.narrative:
Diakonia har ansökt om finansiering av egeninsats om 2 180 000 SEK för EU-projektet "Promoting Civil Society engagement in local government policies and decision making processes in Matabeleland region, Zimbabwe" under 2020-2021.
Insatsen syftar till:
1. "The overall objective is to contribute to enhanced capacity of civil society organisations (CSOs) to meaningfully and constructively participate in local and national policy, legislation and decision making processes; to ensure the fulfilment of civic and socio-economic rights of citizens, including women, youth and other marginalised groups and to promote gender equality, transparency, accountability, social cohesion and resilience in Zimbabwe."
2. "Specific Objective: Three civil society organisations (CSOs) and eleven community based organisations, which promote gender equality and the empowerment of women, men, male and female youth, and persons with disabilities (PwDs), have secured strong institutional capacity to participate meaningfully and constructively in local government policies, legislative and decision making processes and service delivery issues in the selected four rural and four urban local authorities in Matabeleland North and South and Bulawayo provinces."
Projektet kommer att genomföras på lokal nivå i Zimbabwe och Diakonia kommer att arbeta i samverkan med tre civilsamhällesorganisationer, BPRA, SWRGN och WILD. Diakonia är huvudsökande organisation och har det övergripande ansvaret för projektets implementering och koordinering.
Den aktuella insatsen har EU-kommissionens referensnummer CSO-LA/2019/413-607. Insatsen har en total budget på 1 000 000 EUR, vilket motsvarar cirka 10 560 980 SEK. Av detta har Diakonia beviljats 800 000 EUR från EU-kommissionen och ansöker om 2 180 000 SEK (cirka 20%) från Sida.

Diakonia has applied to Sida for funding of 2 180 000 SEK to carry out the EU-project "Promoting Civil Society engagement in local government policies and decision making processes in Matabeleland region, Zimbabwe" during 2020-2021.
The project aims to:
1. "The overall objective is to contribute to enhanced capacity of civil society organisations (CSOs) to meaningfully and constructively participate in local and national policy, legislation and decision making processes; to ensure the fulfilment of civic and socio-economic rights of citizens, including women, youth and other marginalised groups and to promote gender equality, transparency, accountability, social cohesion and resilience in Zimbabwe."
2. "Specific Objective: Three civil society organisations (CSOs) and eleven community based organisations, which promote gender equality and the empowerment of women, men, male and female youth, and persons with disabilities (PwDs), have secured strong institutional capacity to participate meaningfully and constructively in local government policies, legislative and decision making processes and service delivery issues in the selected four rural and four urban local authorities in Matabeleland North and South and Bulawayo provinces."
The project will be conducted on a local level in Zimbabwe and Diakonia will collaborate with three civil society organisations, BPRA, SWRGN and WILD. Diakonia is lead applicant to Sida and has the overall responsibility for the coordination and implementation of the project.
The contribution has the EU Commission reference number: CSO-LA/2019/413-607. The contribution's total budget is 1 000 000 EUR, which corresponds to approximately 10 560 980 SEK. The requested support from Sida is 2 180 000 SEK, which corresponds to 20% of the total budget.

Insatsens övergripande mål: "The overall objective is to contribute to enhanced capacity of civil society organisations (CSOs) to meaningfully and constructively participate in local and national policy, legislation and decision making processes; to ensure the fulfilment of civic and socio-economic rights of citizens, including women, youth and other marginalised groups and to promote gender equality, transparency, accountability, social cohesion and resilience in Zimbabwe."
Insatsens specifika mål: "Three civil society organisations (CSOs) and eleven community based organisations, which promote gender equality and the empowerment of women, men, male and female youth, and persons with disabilities (PwDs), have secured strong institutional capacity to participate meaningfully and constructively in local government policies, legislative and decision making processes and service delivery issues in the selected four rural and four urban local authorities in Matabeleland North and South and Bulawayo provinces."

"The project increased womens participation in local decision-making processes, including policy making, devolution of power and budgeting as constitutional rights. A total of 19 028 women (5 356 aged between18-35; 13 374 aged above 35, and 298 women with disabilities), were sensitised about their constitutional rights and local government processes of planning, budgeting and service delivery issues using different platforms convened by the project. The project strengthened womens capacity to self-mobilise and confidently demand accountability from duty bearers. For example, conscientized women actively participated and made submissions during budget consultation meetings and public hearings on Sexual Harassment Bill and Guardianship of Minors Amendment Bill.
The project strengthened the capacity of Local Authorities in accountability, gender-responsive management and planning to ensure gender-responsive social service delivery and inclusive decision-making. The Local Authorities under the Action namely Bulawayo City Council (BCC), Kusile Rural District Council, Beitbridge Town Council, Lupane and Hwange Town councils established gender committees, gender focal persons and gender desks as part of gender mainstreaming and inclusivity within local authority operations.
The project strengthened citizens confidence to engage local authorities. For example, due to negligence by the local authority in providing safe and portable water for residents, there was an outbreak of water borne typhoid and diarrhoea in Emganwini suburb in Bulawayo. Residents mobilised themselves and engaged Bulawayo City Council to avail alternative means for residents to access safe and clean water to avert further causalities. Following the engagement between the citizens and local authority, the Bulawayo City Council availed water bowsers for the affected areas whilst they rehabilitated the water and sewer system. The local authority also ensured that all affected residents received free treatment at all local authority clinics. Residents in Bulawayo also rejected an unjustified 210% budget increase by Bulawayo City Council in 2021.
Institutional and technical capacity; The project improved internal systems and programming for the CBOs. Through the project, Human Resource policies were developed for Matobo Youth Development Trust and Hope for Children and Youth Foundation. Gender and Social inclusion policies were developed for Maranatha Orphans Care Trust and Souls Comfort. Finance policies and financial procedures manuals were developed for Hope for Children and Youth Foundation and Maranatha Orphans Care Trust. Safeguarding policies were developed for Greater Whange Residents Trust and Hope for Children and Youth Foundation. CBOs such as Matobo Youth Development Trust were assisted in developing a Board Charter to guide Board operations. Support in developing these policies improved internal governance and increased visibility of the organizations such as Youth Invest who attracted funding from OSISA and the Dutch Embassy. Sibanye Animal Welfare and Conservancy Trust (SAWC) adopted a new accounting system called Accmass, thus contributing to strengthened financial management systems and accountability of resources.
The project created synergies between the implementing partners and other CSOs. For example, the implementing partners (IPs) BPRA, SWRGN and WILD partnered with Zimbabwe Lawyers for Human Rights and the Legal Resource Foundation to raise awareness on constitutional provisions relating to citizens civic and socio-economic rights as well as litigation for Rights Holders who were affected by drinking contaminated water supplied by Bulawayo City Council."
